_comment: Pre-existing defects found during the code-organization pass. They are recorded, not fixed, because fixing them changes product behaviour and that is a separate decision. The verify gate fails on anything NOT listed here, so this file must shrink over time — never grow to silence a new break.

unresolvedInlineHandlers.name: triggerResumeUpload
unresolvedInlineHandlers.problem: The 'Upload Resume (PDF)' zone on the Jobs page calls a function that is defined nowhere, so clicking it throws a ReferenceError and nothing happens.
unresolvedInlineHandlers.why_not_fixed: There is no resume-upload endpoint and no file storage anywhere in the backend, and the job-application flow collects a resume URL instead (app.js:5205). Implementing upload would be a new feature; deleting the zone removes a user-visible affordance. Both are product decisions, not refactoring.

securityFindings.title: A donor can mark their own donation as successful
securityFindings.problem: The endpoint authorises on `donor_user_id === req.user.uid`, i.e. it trusts the donor to confirm their own payment, and `success` defaults to true when the body omits it. Any authenticated user can POST to this route for their own pending donation and have it written as status SUCCESS with a receipt code, without any money moving. That also inflates the campaign totals and the donor leaderboard.
securityFindings.why_not_fixed: Correct confirmation has to come from the payment gateway, not the browser — a signed bKash/Nagad/card webhook, or a service-role route keyed on a per-transaction token the gateway issues. That is a new integration and a change to how donations settle, so it needs a product decision rather than a refactor.
securityFindings.preexisting: Yes — byte-identical at main:routes_v2.js:486-494. Carried over unchanged.

securityFindings.title: Event ticket signatures fall back to a hardcoded key
securityFindings.problem: `crypto.createHmac('sha256', ENCRYPTION_KEY || 'dic-ticket')`. If ENCRYPTION_KEY is unset the tickets are signed with the constant 'dic-ticket', which is in the source, so anyone can forge a valid ticket signature and check in.
securityFindings.why_not_fixed: The fix is to fail closed when no key is configured — the same stance the identity-vault endpoints already take via `encryptionReady`. Doing that would stop ticket issuance on any deployment currently running without ENCRYPTION_KEY, so it needs to be sequenced with setting the key in the environment.
securityFindings.preexisting: Yes — byte-identical at main:routes_v2.js:161. Carried over unchanged.

securityFindings.title: Two endpoints return data to unauthenticated callers
securityFindings.problem: Both answer 200 with real rows and no token. Verified live: chapter members returns alumni names and ids; the planner endpoint returns an event's budgets, committees, sponsors, tasks and volunteers. Every sibling route in those families requires authentication.
securityFindings.why_not_fixed: Adding requireAuth changes the API contract for any caller relying on the current behaviour, so it is flagged for approval rather than applied silently.
securityFindings.preexisting: Yes — visible in the pre-refactor contract baseline.

securityFindings.title: 500 responses leak internal error text
securityFindings.problem: `ok()` returns `err.message` to the client, so a failed query can expose SQL text, column names and constraint names.
securityFindings.why_not_fixed: Behaviour preserved deliberately during the refactor. The fix is to log the detail server-side and return a generic message, which changes every 500 body.
securityFindings.preexisting: Yes — identical in all four original copies of ok().

securityFindings.title: Database TLS certificate verification is disabled
securityFindings.problem: The pool accepts any certificate, so the connection is not protected against an active man-in-the-middle.
securityFindings.why_not_fixed: Carried over verbatim from db.js. Enabling verification needs the provider CA to be trusted first, which is an environment change.

securityFindings.title: Vercel still serves backend source statically
securityFindings.problem: The Express allow-list in src/server/middleware/static-assets.js closes source disclosure for the Node server, but on Vercel the CDN serves the repository root itself before the function runs, so /server.js and similar may still be fetchable in production.
securityFindings.why_not_fixed: The fix is to move the web assets into a public/ directory (Vercel then serves only that) or add a .vercelignore. Either changes deployment layout, which the user explicitly chose to keep unchanged in this pass.
